I am 50 years old. I never went to school. I learned everything from my father and from watching the neighbors. My farm is 10.9 mu. I keep 7 mu for wheat and maize — wheat in the fall, then maize right after harvest. The rest is vegetables: 1.5 mu watermelon, 1.2 mu tomato, and 1.2 mu eggplant. There are only two of us in the house, so that is all the vegetable land we can handle.

For wheat, last year I spread one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing. When the wheat turned green in spring, I put 20 kilograms of urea per mu. At heading I put another 10 kilograms. That gave me about 480 kilograms per mu. This year I will do exactly the same. I water four times: green-up, jointing, heading, and grain filling. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once. I use improved seeds from the shop.

For maize, as soon as the wheat is cut in June, I plant hybrid seeds without plowing — no time to waste, and the machine can plant through the stubble. I put 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer in the row per mu. When the plants are knee-high, I spread 25 kilograms of urea per mu. I water twice if the summer is dry. I spray once for weeds and once for corn borer. Last year I got about 520 kilograms per mu.

Vegetables need more money and more work. For tomatoes, I rotary-till the soil fine and plant hybrid seedlings. I put two 50-kilogram bags of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then I topdress with urea and potassium fertilizer twice. I water ten times and spray seven times for blight and whiteflies. I hope for 3,500 kilograms per mu. Eggplant gets the same: two bags of compound base, then urea and potassium later. I water eight times and spray six times. Expected yield is 3,000 kilograms per mu.

Watermelon needs potassium for sweet fruit. I put one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu and extra potassium sulfate. I water six times and spray four times. I expect 2,200 kilograms per mu.

I spend my own money on every bag. I worry about costs. But a bad harvest is worse than wasting a little fertilizer. I would rather put a bit too much than risk losing yield. I watch Old Wang and the others. If they use more fertilizer this year, I will use more too. Change is risky, so I mostly do what I did last year.
